Central line care. Assisting with insertion, maintenance and removal, step by step.
Step one. Know the central lines: P I C C lines, tunnelled and non-tunnelled catheters, and implantable ports. Know their indications, the insertion sites, and when C V P monitoring is needed.

Step two. Know the risks. Use aseptic technique in every phase. The central line bundle reduces catheter related bloodstream infections. Watch for air embolism, occlusion, and site infection, and act on early signs.

Step three. To prepare, check the physician's order. Explain the procedure, to the family if the patient is unconscious, and make sure consent is obtained. Assemble the equipment, set up the transducer, ensure privacy and the correct position, and perform hand hygiene.
Step four. Critical point. Use a full sterile barrier: hand hygiene, sterile gloves, a gown, a head cover, a face mask, and a face shield or eye protection. Start the central line bundle.
Step five. Critical point. With sterile technique, pour chlorhexidine two percent in seventy percent alcohol, and normal saline, into the tray. Open extra items onto the sterile drape.

Step six. During insertion, keep the patient comfortable and monitor vital signs and heart rhythm. Clean the site and let the antiseptic air-dry completely. Secure the catheter and apply a transparent dressing. Then arrange a chest X-ray, reposition the patient, and perform hand hygiene.
Step seven. Check the site for bleeding or haematoma every fifteen to thirty minutes for the first two hours.
Step eight. To flush, use a ten millilitre syringe, which gives lower pressure. Use a pulsatile push, pause technique, clamp with positive pressure, and flush every lumen regularly.

Step nine. Critical point. For a blood sample, perform hand hygiene, wear gloves, and set up a sterile field. Stop IV fluids for one minute, after confirming with the physician. Clamp the lumen, the brown port is preferred, remove the cap, and scrub the port for thirty seconds with chlorhexidine and alcohol. Let it dry for thirty to sixty seconds.

Step ten. Withdraw five millilitres and discard it, to clear the dead space. With a new ten millilitre syringe, draw the samples. Then flush with ten millilitres of normal saline using positive pressure, and reclamp.

Step eleven. Critical point. For a Vascath heparin lock, flush with saline first, then instil heparin as per the manufacturer. The lock prevents clots while the catheter is not in use, and keeps the lumen patent.

Step twelve. To remove the line, position the patient and time the removal with their breathing, as per policy, to prevent air embolism. Remove the dressing and sutures, pull with steady, constant pressure, then apply direct pressure for five to ten minutes, and apply a dressing. Check the catheter is complete and intact.
Step thirteen. Protect the sterile field, communicate clearly with the patient, family and team, and stay calm and accountable in emergencies.

Step fourteen. Document the indication, the insertion, and every dressing, flush and cap change. Record site signs, report complications promptly, educate the patient, and hand over at every shift change.
Watch, take the quiz, then get signed off.
